text: Anna is a guilty pleasure, delivering just enough cheese/sleaze to satisfy a viewer’s baser instincts but wrapping it all up in a clever storytelling style that keeps us on our toes and guessing.
Besson’s new film is an overly smug repackaging of his most acclaimed work, La Femme Nikita.
Watching Anna, one imagines that director Luc Besson saw both Atomic Blonde (2017) and Red Sparrow (2018) and then decided to put his spin on the beautiful Russian spy movie.
An auteur tackling a genre movie with aplomb.
While director's approach and visuals remain energetic, his ideas now qualify as tired.
Anna mines familiar stereotypes without adding anything new to the genre.
It's a dull, self-parodial espionage thriller in which clichés, hollow characters, and action sequences abound that put me in a state of absolute indifference. [Full review in Spanish]
Any sense of empowerment in this female-led spy thriller is lost amidst a hanging fog of poor decisions and cardboard characters.
